title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a market prices a business at forty times trailing earnings, it is no longer paying for what the factory built yesterday—it is underwriting the next decade of execution.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk

web_blocks.html: At the November 23, 2026 NSE close of ₹7,895.00 [28], Garware Hi-Tech Films (GRWRHITECH) has a market cap of ₹18,340 Cr across 2.323 crore shares [1]. On November 25, 2026, live TradingView data pulled back -3.38% to ₹7,628.00 (₹17,740 Cr on Screener) [1][28]. Net of ₹933 Cr cash (Sep 30, 2026) [25] and ₹28.29 Cr in lease and acceptance debt [32] (zero long-term debt [33]), enterprise value is ₹17,435 Cr at ₹7,895.00 (₹16,835 Cr at ₹7,628.00). TTM net profit is ₹426 Cr (EPS ₹183.41) and TTM operating profit is ₹547 Cr [1]. The stock thus trades at 43.0x TTM P/E and 6.31x P/B (BV ₹1,251) at ₹7,895.00, or 41.6x P/E and 6.10x P/B at ₹7,628.00 [1][28]. EV/TTM Operating EBITDA stands at 31.9x at ₹7,895.00 (30.8x at ₹7,628.00).

Why does the market pay 41.6x–43.0x trailing earnings when Indian packaging peers trade at 5x to 10x? Investors are pricing the profit surge underway rather than legacy BOPET history. GRWRHITECH rallied from ₹2,690.70 to ₹8,079.50 [28] as H1 FY27 sales jumped 25% YoY to ₹1,329 Cr and PAT rose 50% YoY to ₹262 Cr [25]. Annualizing H1 FY27 PAT—allowing for Q3 seasonal softness [23]—points to ₹490–520 Cr in FY27E PAT (EPS ₹211–₹224). That sets forward P/E at 35.3x–37.4x FY27E at ₹7,895.00 (34.1x–36.2x at ₹7,628.00). If the Lubrizol TPU line adds 150–200 bps in FY28 [24] and the ₹191 Cr SCF line opens in H1 FY28 [23], FY28E PAT of ₹600–640 Cr lowers two-year forward P/E to 28.7x–30.6x.

web_blocks.caption: Reverse DCF Implied Expectations at 2026-11-23 Close ₹7,895.00 (EV ₹17,435 Cr, WACC 11.5%, Terminal Growth 5.0%)
web_blocks.takeaway: At the 2026-11-23 close of ₹7,895.00, the market prices in ~18.2% annual FCF compounding for a decade (17.5% at live ₹7,628). Our ₹7,250–₹7,650 support zone still sits 28.1%–35.2% above Conservative DCF value (₹5,660).

web_blocks.html: Our Reverse DCF makes valuation discipline clear. We use an 11.5% WACC (zero long-term debt, 51% US sales) [2][33] and a 5.0% terminal growth rate. At ₹17,435 Cr EV, free cash flow must grow ~18.2% a year for ten years. That goal is reachable if sales grow ~20% with >27% EBITDA margins [24] and building films scale toward ₹1,000 Cr. Yet Pass 1 blind spots add two clear guardrails. First, DGTR found under 25% total Indian PPF share and CY24 domestic PPF losses under 200%–300% Chinese undercutting [29]. Finance Ministry duty enactment also remains unverified [30]. Second, FY26 notes flag ₹215.74 Cr in contingencies and commitments—including an unprovided ₹18.37 Cr tax dispute—plus component auditors on foreign units (~36% of sales) [31]. Buying at ₹7,895.00 pays full fare up front with zero cushion.

web_blocks.caption: Indian Specialty & Packaging Films Peer Valuation & Return Comparison (Live Snapshot: Nov 2026)
web_blocks.takeaway: GRWRHITECH trades at 41.6x Screener P/E (43.0x at 2026-11-23 close ₹7,895) versus 4.9x–9.3x for UFLEX and COSMOFIRST, earning its premium through 18.1% headline ROCE (>28% ex-cash) and 28.7% H1 FY27 EBITDA margins versus 7.0%–11.2% ROCE among commodity packaging peers.

web_blocks.html: The peer table shows why simple P/E screens misread Garware Hi-Tech Films. Commodity BOPET and BOPP mills face global oversupply near 54% utilization [18]. UFlex trades at 4.87x Screener P/E (4.92x TV) with 7.03% ROCE and 1.26x debt-to-equity. Cosmo First trades at 9.27x Screener P/E (9.47x TV) with 11.2% ROCE and 0.91x debt-to-equity, and broke below its 20D, 50D, and 30W moving averages [1][28]. Polyplex and Jindal Poly face even weaker returns [18][19]. By contrast, GRWRHITECH gets 75% of Q2 FY27 sales from SCF (51%) and PPF (24%) [23]. It holds zero long-term debt [32][33] and earns 54%–60% gross margins—1,000 to 1,500 bps above global peer XPEL, Inc. [16][17].

web_blocks.title: Valuation Discipline: Premium Franchise, Thin Margin of Safety Above Support
paragraphs: At ₹7,895.00, GRWRHITECH trades at 43.0x trailing earnings and ~29x–31x FY28E earnings. Our 12–18 month Base target stays ₹9,300 (+17.8% from ₹7,895; +21.6% from ₹7,650), yet Conservative DCF (₹5,660) forbids chasing highs.

web_blocks.mechanism: PPF and window film brand re-rated to 50x–70x P/E during the post-COVID aftermarket boom as investors extrapolated 30%+ growth indefinitely; when US dealership attach rates normalized and China/EV OEM shifts slowed top-line growth to single digits in 2024, the multiple compressed by >55% despite resilient gross margins.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Stock fell from $103 peak (2021) to ~$34 (2024) — a 67% drawdown even as revenue still grew from $259M to ~$420M.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even genuine PPF compounders suffer severe multiple compression when priced above 40x trailing P/E if growth decelerates or tariffs bite. Entry discipline at technical support matters as much as business quality.

web_blocks.html: Reconciling Book Value, Cash Drag & Contingent Footnotes: At 6.31x Price-to-Book (6.10x at live ₹7,628) [1][28], value screens often skip GRWRHITECH. Strip out ₹933 Cr of cash [25] and add ₹28.29 Cr of lease debt [32]. Operating EV is ₹17,435 Cr at ₹7,895.00 (₹16,835 Cr at ₹7,628.00), or ~31x–32x trailing EBITDA. Unverified ADD enactment [30] and ₹215.74 Cr of contingencies [31] reinforce our refusal to chase above ₹7,650.

Valuation Trigger: Buying inside ₹7,250–₹7,650 cuts entry valuation to ~26.4x–27.8x FY28E EPS (₹275) and restores 1.65:1 base asymmetry to ₹9,300 (stop ₹6,650). Renewed US tariffs (>25%) or EBITDA margins below 22% would cut fair value toward ₹6,100.

book_paragraphs: Now that we have audited the Waluj factory floor, the Lubrizol TPU extrusion project, the DGTR domestic PPF anti-dumping reality, and the FY26 audit footnotes without looking at a single stock price, we unlock the market screen and ask the central valuation question: at the verified November 23, 2026 close of ₹7,895.00—and even after the November 25 intraday pullback to ₹7,628.00—what is Mr. Market already pricing into Garware Hi-Tech Films?

Let us walk through the arithmetic cleanly. Across 2.323 crore shares, ₹7,895.00 values the equity at ₹18,340 crore, while the live November 25 pull to ₹7,628.00 puts Screener market capitalization at ₹17,740 crore. Subtract ₹933 crore of cash and liquid investments reported as of September 30, 2026, and add back ₹28.29 crore of total FY26 lease liabilities and acceptances verified by CARE Ratings, and enterprise value comes to ₹17,435 crore at the November 23 close—or ₹16,835 crore at ₹7,628.00. Against trailing twelve-month net profit of ₹426 crore and operating EBITDA of ₹547 crore, the market demands 43.0 times trailing earnings at ₹7,895.00, easing to 41.6 times at ₹7,628.00.

Compared with domestic packaging peers—UFlex at 4.9 times earnings with 7.0% ROCE and 1.26 times debt-to-equity, or Cosmo First at 9.3 times earnings with 11.2% ROCE and a broken technical trend—41.6 to 43.0 times looks expensive on a naive screen. The gap exists because Garware vacated the commodity BOPET battlefield. Seventy-five percent of Q2 FY27 sales came from Sun Control Films and Paint Protection Films, generating a 28.7% H1 FY27 EBITDA margin and an ex-cash, ex-revaluation ROCE north of 28% with zero long-term debt.

Yet deserving a premium multiple does not mean paying any price. Running a Reverse DCF on ₹17,435 crore of enterprise value with an 11.5% discount rate and a 5.0% terminal growth rate shows that ₹7,895.00 requires normalized free cash flow to compound at roughly 18.2% per year for a full decade while holding 27.5% to 28.5% EBITDA margins. Even at ₹7,628.00, the implied hurdle is 17.5% annual free cash flow compounding for ten years.

Can Garware clear that bar? H1 FY27 revenue rose 25% to ₹1,329 crore and PAT climbed 50% to ₹262 crore, putting FY27E PAT on pace for ₹490 to ₹520 crore. Once the Q3 FY27 Lubrizol TPU line and H1 FY28 automated SCF line ramp, FY28E PAT of ₹600 to ₹640 crore compresses the two-year forward P/E toward 28 to 31 times. Still, our Pass 1 blind-spot audit adds essential humility. DGTR's June 2026 Final Findings revealed that Garware held less than 25% total domestic Indian PPF market share and booked domestic PPF losses in CY2024 under 200% to 300% Chinese price undercutting, while Finance Ministry Customs notification of the recommended anti-dumping duty remains unverified as of November 2026. Add ₹215.74 crore in contingent liabilities and commitments—including an unprovided ₹18.37 crore disputed tax demand—and overseas component-auditor reliance covering 36% of consolidated revenue, and you see why buying at 43 times trailing earnings leaves zero margin for error.

Remember XPEL in the United States between 2021 and 2024. XPEL was an undisputed PPF category leader whose revenue still grew from $259 million to roughly $420 million, yet its stock plunged 67% from $103 to $34 when a 50x-plus multiple met slower dealership attach rates. Great polymer franchises still experience violent valuation compression whenever execution hiccups meet an extended entry price.

Let us check the forward asymmetry math. If Garware executes our Base Case—delivering roughly ₹2,600 crore of FY27 revenue at a 27% EBITDA margin and scaling FY28 EPS toward ₹275—applying a steady-state 33.8 times multiple yields our ₹9,300 base target over 12 to 18 months. From the verified November 23 close of ₹7,895.00, ₹9,300 offers just +17.8% upside against -15.8% downside to our ratcheted ₹6,650 structural stop—a weak 1.13-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. From our ₹7,250 to ₹7,650 support entry zone, however, ₹9,300 delivers +21.6% to +28.3% upside against -8.3% to -13.1% risk, restoring an earned 1.65-to-1 asymmetry at the top of the band.

Even after crediting ₹933 crore of cash at full face value, paying ₹7,895.00 means valuing the operating franchise at roughly 32 times trailing operating EBITDA. Nothing in our Reverse DCF rules out strong multi-year compounding if TPU backward integration adds 150 to 200 basis points to margins and architectural films scale cleanly. What the valuation math insists upon is patience: separate admiration for the factory from discipline at the order ticket, and wait for price and confirmation inside ₹7,250 to ₹7,650.

Let us also run a concrete margin-normalization stress test so we know our exact downside before committing another rupee. Suppose Q1 FY27's 30.3% operating margin was a seasonal summer peak and full-year EBITDA margins mean-revert from our 27.0% base assumption back to FY26's 23.6%—perhaps because Chinese TPU PPF price undercutting persists without a Finance Ministry anti-dumping notification or because US freight and warehouse costs stay elevated. Under that 23.6% margin scenario, FY28E EPS drops from roughly ₹275 down to ₹240.37. Even if the market still awards a 33.8 times multiple, the stock's fair value slips to ₹8,125—leaving just 0.48-to-1 asymmetry from ₹7,650. And if the multiple compresses to 25 times alongside slower growth, fair value falls to ₹6,009, right in line with our ₹6,100 bear case.

That single sensitivity check explains why we anchor every decision to our support band rather than chasing 52-week highs. At ₹7,895.00, the upside-to-downside ratio is skewed against you. Inside ₹7,250 to ₹7,650, however, your entry multiple compresses to 26.4 to 27.8 times FY28E earnings, giving you room to absorb a normal quarterly wobble without losing structural conviction.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The hardest discipline in quality investing is refusing to overpay for a genuine compounder. At ₹7,895.00 (43.0x trailing P/E), Garware is pricing in 18.2% annual FCF compounding for ten years with zero cushion for unenacted Indian PPF duties or US tariff swings. Waiting for confirmed support inside ₹7,250–₹7,650 restores a 1.65:1 risk-reward profile.
